mstts:express-as.prosody: As we wrap up, I want you to remember this—if you've ever felt weighed down by resistance, by those doubts or distractions that make you want to put things off, you're honestly not alone. The war of art? It's a battle that everyone faces, anyone who's ever tried to create, to make a difference, or to pursue something meaningful. The lessons are simple, but let’s be honest, they aren’t always easy. They call for courage, patience, and a willingness to start over, one day at a time. So, what does this mean for you? First, resistance is something we all deal with—and in fact, it gets even stronger when the work really matters. But here’s the good news: discipline and routine? They actually create the space for inspiration to show up. And you don’t have to go it alone. Having a community, finding support—those things are absolutely essential if you want to stay committed to your creative path. And when you hit setbacks or even fail, it’s not the end. It’s just another part of the journey. Every step you take shapes you. This creative path is about growing, transforming, and discovering more about who you are—over a lifetime. Here’s what I hope you’ll take with you: the struggle you feel? It’s not weakness. It’s proof of your courage. Every time you show up and push through the doubt or fear, you’re building something more valuable than any finished piece—you’re building yourself. The world truly needs your voice, your ideas, your unique touch. Don’t wait for things to feel perfect, or for resistance to just vanish. Start right where you are. Use what you have. Trust that by showing up, again and again, you’ll find your way. And remember, you’re not walking this path alone. Others have faced these same challenges and kept going, just like you can. Yes, the journey’s long and the obstacles are real—but so are the rewards. So keep going. Every day you choose to fight, you move closer to the life you’re meant to live.
